claims.head: What happened to the Canadiens’ chance quality?
claims.body: Taken over this season and last, the Canadiens are around the middle of the league for chance quality. Look at this season alone, though, and they’ve been settling for worse looks. We think tonight looks more like this season’s Canadiens.
claims.nums: Chance quality: 12th over two seasons (6.5% a shot), 20th this season (6.1% a shot)
claims.gist: The Canadiens aren’t the team you remember for chance quality.
claims.call: The Canadiens’ chance quality is worse than their blended level of 6.5% a shot.

claims.head: A shadow job for Robertson, Hintz and Seguin
claims.call: The Stars’ L2 (Robertson, Hintz and Seguin) spends at least 51% of its 5-on-5 time against the Canadiens’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Stars keep sending Robertson’s line (Robertson, Hintz and Seguin) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Glen Gulutzan has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Canadiens’ first line is Caufield, Suzuki and Slafkovský.
claims.nums: At home: 51% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 34% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Glen Gulutzan likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Canadiens’ first line.

claims.body: The Stars’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Canadiens’ kill is around the middle. Every trip to the box hurts the Canadiens more than most.

notes.text: Nick Suzuki is out (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Oliver Kapanen has taken his spot beside Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovský.

Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Kirby Dach has taken his spot beside Alex Newhook and Juraj Slafkovský.
Mike Matheson returned in their last game after missing 4 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Owen Beck was added to the roster on Oct 14 and has played beside Jake Evans and Kirby Dach.
David Reinbacher was added to the roster on Oct 15.
Owen Beck was added to the roster on Oct 23 and has played beside Jake Evans and Kirby Dach.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, up from 6% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Esa Lindell is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Thomas Harley has taken his spot beside Miro Heiskanen.
Matt Duchene is on long-term injured reserve (abdomen injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.

DAL.head: The matchup suits the Stars
DAL.body: Even though Dallas will be without Lindell, the Stars have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage, and Montréal will be without Suzuki. The Canadiens can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

MTL.head: The Canadiens have a hill to climb
MTL.body: Even though Dallas will be without Lindell, the Stars have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage, and Montréal will be without Suzuki. The Canadiens can pull it off if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: A measuring-stick game
paras: The Stars have won four straight. The Canadiens are 5-3-2. Two good teams meet.

It’s strength against strength: the Canadiens are near the top of the league for shot volume, but the Stars are one of the best at keeping shots away. The Habs aren’t the team you remember for chance quality.

items.text: Chris Kreider has a point in six straight games against Dallas.
The Canadiens are newly without Nick Suzuki, and have been without Samuel Montembeault and Ivan Demidov for several games. Jacob Fowler is expected to start.
The Stars are newly without Esa Lindell, and have had to make do without Matt Duchene all season.
Jason Robertson has four goals in six games against Montréal since 2023-24.
